newsitem.title: USA: FIA URGES PROGRESS IN CME/CBOT COMMON CLEARING.
newsitem.headline: FIA URGES PROGRESS IN CME/CBOT COMMON CLEARING.

text.p: The Futures Industry Association (FIA) is proposing new ideas it hopes would spur progress in common clearing for two of the world's biggest futures exchanges in Chicago, FIA President John Damgard said on Thursday.
"We're suggesting some new concepts that we think will bridge the gap that sometimes become a stumbling block between the two exchanges," Damgard told Reuters.
Damgard, in Chicago to meet leaders of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) and the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), declined to disclose the details of the proposal.
"We're out here to meet with both the Merc and the Board of Trade to ascertain the seriousness of each of the institutions," he said.

The CBOT and CME had renewed discussions to merge operations, including clearing, in January 1996. Common clearing would benefit trading firms by reducing strain on back-office functions and margin requirements.

However, the CME-CBOT Joint Strategics Initiatives Committee ran into roadblocks earlier in the year after a study they commissioned showed that merging the exchanges' clearing hardware may actually incur prohibitive cost.

"You look at the securities industry with one clearing house and you look at the options industry with one clearing house," Damgard said. "We simply can no longer afford to have stand-alone clearing houses next to each and every exchange. It is simply inefficient and the cost saving...is imperative."
The FIA has set up a committee, headed by Morgan Stanley's John Davidson, to deal with the issue, Damgard noted.

"It was John Davidson's wish to meet face-to-face with leaders of both exchanges and to be very certain that we aren't going to be wasting a lot of time on yet another study of common clearing," he said.
The FIA delegation met with CME leaders on Wednesday and was due to meet CBOT executives later on Thursday.
"The discussions were very constructive and the dialogue continues," CME chairman emeritus Leo Melamed told Reuters.
He added that everyone agreed on the goal, but that "common clearing issues have been difficult."
Melamed said no model had been chosen for it nor any timetable set. But one CBOT source said the FIA was proposing that the Chicago exchanges model their clearing on a system used in London.
Damgard made clear that a new system must satisfy all customers and must be free from each exchange's interest.
"A new clearing corp...would be free to operate in a fashion not connected to the politics of either exchange," Damgard said.
Many FIA members were also in the securities business and used one clearing house facilitating trades on the New York Stock Exchange, the American Stock Exchange and Nasdaq over- the-counter market.
"These (exchanges) are avid competitors and yet clearing is something that's apart from competition," he said.
